_comment: Mutation testing targets the modules where a silently wrong branch is dangerous: URL validation, SSRF protection, scoring/evaluation, secret redaction and the benchmark orchestration. Running it over jsdom parsing or the SDK adapters would multiply the runtime without testing anything a unit test does not already pin down. The command runner is used instead of the vitest runner because @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner 10 does not drive Vitest 5 correctly here: it reports 0 tests run per mutant, so every mutant survives regardless of test quality. The command runner activates mutants through __STRYKER_ACTIVE_MUTANT__, which the instrumented code reads, and is version-independent. The per-mutant command runs the unit and security suites: those are the suites that exercise these modules, and running the integration/spec/regression suites for every mutant would multiply the wall time for a handful of extra kills.
